Three of the four design axes fail (`completeness`, `decision_clarity`, `executability`). `recoverability` is the fourth one and I scored it FAIL as well, which goes beyond the axes the fixture's original gate failed:

- **`decision_clarity`, `executability`:** these fail for the same two reasons the original gate gave. The plan never picks between retrying with raised permissions and committing locally only. It also never decides whether status checks are supported when cmux is absent, or what happens if they aren't.
- **`completeness`:** constraint C-1 (keep the checkpoint commit format) is never linked to a work item, risk or scenario. The cmux assumption that was never checked also has no matching risk entry.
- **`recoverability`:** the plan has no install or verification order and no recovery path if the change goes wrong.

The original gate scored these last two PASS, so this gives two more FAILs than that baseline. I kept them because the plan documents really don't cover them.
